messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Deducer - ggplot2 gsoc progress
parts:
For those who are interested I'm keeping a screen cast vlog of the development progress of the Deducer-ggplot2 GUI that is being developed over the summer. Updates will be posted on the R google summer of code blog. The first post has just gone up:

http://gsoc2010r.wordpress.com/2010/06/19/ggplot2-gui-progress/

The main point of this project is to create an elegant, and easy to use interface for building and sharing statistical graphics. It is being designed to be easy enough for beginners, and flexible enough for experts.

 Ian

messages.subject: Re: Deducer - ggplot2 gsoc progress
parts:
Nice, looking really useful.

Three comments:

Do you plan to have a 'reveal code' window? I think it would really help learning if the code showed layers being added as R commands.

I'm not a huge hidden tray fan, I suppose one can have an option to see the controls all the time.

One of the things that newcomers (and old hands) have trouble with it realizing that ggplot2 becomes a lot easier when data is in the right format, anything that the GUI can do to help with that really would be fantastic.

But hey, that's just words from the peanut gallery.

:)

--J

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Deducer - ggplot2 gsoc progress
parts:
James,

Thanks for the comments.

1. I didn't say so explicitly, but when you click Run, the ggplot2
code gets sent to the R console, where you can view and edit it. I'm a
big believer in having the code be transparent and reproducible.

2. The issue is that there are 31 geoms, so displaying them all
without dominating the GUI's real estate is difficult. Without the
tray you'd spend all your time scrolling. If it was always kept down,
you'd have trouble viewing the plot.

3. Deducer has quite a lot of data manipulation dialogs (e.g.
subsetting transforming, merging, and recoding). You can view them at:
http://www.deducer.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php?n=Main.DeducerManual .
Hopeful this summer I'll be adding two dialogs for reshaping data
frames, which would be important for many of the types of ggplot2
preprocessing steps.

I welcome all peanut gallery comments. Feedback is vital for
development.


Cheers,
Ian
